record.paper_title: Solutions to open problems of Yang concerning inverse nodal problems
record.context_brief: Inverse nodal problem for Sturm-Liouville operators
record.original_question: Consider the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem L(q, α, β) on (0,1), given by -y''(x) + q(x)y(x) = λy(x) with real-valued q in L¹(0,1) and boundary conditions y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0 and y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0. Fix b in (1/2,1]. If one knows a subset of the nodal set of eigenfunctions inside (0,b) that is dense in (0,b), but not necessarily s-dense there, is that weaker dense nodal data still sufficient to determine the left boundary parameter α uniquely?

evidence.quote: Open problem I: It is open if the boundary parameter α = α can be determined by a dense subset of the nodal set in (0, b) but not necessarily by an s-dense subset of the nodal set in (0, b).

Remark 3.1: In [6], Cheng et al. improved Yang’s theorem (Theorem 2.1 in [19]) by weakening s-dense conditions instead of dense conditions. The open problem I is answered affirmatively by Cheng et al. (see Theorem 3.2 in [6]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sturm-Liouville boundary value problem L(q,α,β) on the interval (0,1):

  -y''(x) + q(x) y(x) = λ y(x),  x ∈ (0,1),

with real-valued potential q ∈ L¹(0,1), and separated boundary conditions

  y(0) cos α + y'(0) sin α = 0,
  y(1) cos β + y'(1) sin β = 0,

where α ∈ [0,π) and β ∈ (0,π]. For each eigenvalue λ_n let y_n be a corresponding eigenfunction, and let X_n = { x_{n,k} : 1 ≤ k ≤ n−1 } ⊂ (0,1) denote its nodal set (the zeros of y_n in (0,1)). The total nodal set is X = ⋃_n X_n.

Fix b ∈ (1/2, 1]. A subset S ⊂ X ∩ (0,b) is called dense in (0,b) if its closure contains [0,b]. (A stronger notion, "s-dense", requires that for every x ∈ (0,b) there is a sequence x_{n_j, k_j} ∈ S with k_j/n_j → x as j → ∞.)

Question: Suppose one is given only a subset S of the nodal set X ∩ (0,b) that is dense in (0,b), but not necessarily s-dense there. Is this dense (but not necessarily s-dense) nodal data sufficient to determine the left boundary parameter α uniquely? That is, if L(q,α,β) and L(q̃,α̃,β̃) share such a common dense nodal subset in (0,b), must α = α̃?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was answered affirmatively: a dense (not necessarily s-dense) subset of the nodal set in (0,b) with b ∈ (1/2,1] suffices to uniquely determine the left boundary parameter α. This resolution is attributed to Cheng et al., who strengthened the earlier nodal uniqueness theorem by weakening the s-dense hypothesis to a dense hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Solutions to open problems of Yang concerning inverse nodal problems
status_evidence.snippet: The open problem I is answered affirmatively by Cheng et al. (see Theorem 3.2 in [6]).
status_evidence.claim: The dense-nodal-subset version of the uniqueness problem for the boundary parameter α has been resolved affirmatively.
